**Observations:**
- **Rows 0 and 27.** Weights here (inputs 0–27 and 756–783) stay at initialisation size, about ±0.03. These pixels are almost always black.
- **Rows 1 and 2.** Large weights already appear here. For example, inputs 33–41 (row 1, columns 5–13) reach about ±0.15 to ±0.26, and inputs around 60–67 (row 2) reach about ±0.3 to ±0.39.
- **Rows 25–26.** Large weights also appear near the bottom of the frame.
- **Side edges.** Large weights reach columns 1–3 and 24–26 in many rows, which is the full width of the frame.
- **Overall pattern.** Ink therefore regularly fills almost the whole 28×28 frame. The hidden units are broad, blob-like templates, not thin stroke detectors: large coherent regions of one sign, with left/right edge columns and top/bottom bands weighted differently.
- **Unit 5.** Its strongest positive weights are in a low, horizontal band (roughly rows 20–25, left-centre columns). In W2 it is the strongest input to class 9 (+1.70) and also feeds class 5 (+0.60). Its weights to classes 4 and 8 are strongly negative.
- **Unit 3.** It is strongly negative for classes 6 and 1. It is positive for class 9 (+0.99) and class 8 (+0.71).
- **Unit 4.** It favours class 8 (+1.21) and disfavours classes 0, 4 and 7.

**Reasoning:**
- **Not MNIST.** The inputs are 28×28 grayscale with 10 classes, so MNIST-family datasets are the natural candidates. But MNIST digits sit in a centred 20×20 box, so their rows 1–3 and edge columns would keep near-zero, initialisation-level weights. Here those regions carry large, structured weights.
- **Not CIFAR-style data.** Natural images would make every border pixel informative, including row 0 and row 27, which are not here.
- **Fits Fashion-MNIST.** Shirts, pullovers and coats span nearly the full width. Trousers and dresses span nearly the full height. Footwear occupies low, wide horizontal bands. This matches the weight layout.
- **Output layer fits too.** A low-horizontal-band unit (unit 5) drives classes 9 and 5, which would be ankle boot and sandal. Separate units distinguish the upper-body garments (classes 0, 2, 4, 6) from bag (class 8).
- **KMNIST is the main alternative.** It would also use more of the frame, but the large, smooth, garment-shaped templates fit Fashion-MNIST better.

**Dataset:** Fashion-MNIST (Zalando article images, 28×28 grayscale).

**Classes:**
- 0 T-shirt/top
- 1 Trouser
- 2 Pullover
- 3 Dress
- 4 Coat
- 5 Sandal
- 6 Shirt
- 7 Sneaker
- 8 Bag
- 9 Ankle boot

**Confidence:** 72%
